system_description.narrative_title: U.S. moves to secure control/access to Venezuelan oil
system_description.narrative_summary: A coherent narrative across the window is that the U.S. (Trump administration and U.S. firms) is negotiating to secure long‑term access to — and in some accounts partial control of — Venezuela's vast oil reserves through deals, investments, and asset transfers. This initiative is presented as an energy‑security and geopolitical maneuver that alters market expectations, provokes Venezuelan political backlash, and sits alongside related energy geopolitics (e.g., talks over the Strait of Hormuz).
system_description.scope: Inside the system: U.S. executive policy decisions and diplomatic negotiations; Venezuelan oil reserves, producing assets and domestic political actors; U.S. and international oil companies (Chevron, others) and potential asset transactions/investments; oil-market price signals and trader expectations; regional diplomatic reactions. Processes included: deal negotiation, asset transfer/management, market pricing, political denouncement, and maritime-security negotiations.
system_description.super_system: Global energy geopolitics and international security/economic order
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil market and price formation
Maritime chokepoints and regional security (Strait of Hormuz)
Latin American geopolitical alignments and domestic politics
International oil & gas corporate M&A and investment flows
evidence_headlines: US nears deal to secure long-term access to Venezuela's oil reserves, sources say

variables.name: Control share of reserves
variables.description: Proportion of a jurisdiction's proven oil reserves that are effectively controlled or managed by external actors.

variables.name: Foreign investment rate into oil assets
variables.description: Pace at which external capital is invested into a jurisdiction's upstream oil assets and projects.

variables.name: Energy asset transfer flow
variables.description: Rate of ownership transfers and formal asset reassignments of oil-field and related infrastructure.

variables.name: Oil production capacity
variables.description: Maximum sustained physical oil output the production infrastructure can deliver.

variables.name: Oil export volume
variables.description: Volume of crude oil and condensate shipped out of a jurisdiction per unit time.

variables.name: Oil price expectations
variables.description: Market consensus and trader expectations about future oil price levels over relevant horizons.

variables.name: Geopolitical risk to energy supply
variables.description: Overall environmental likelihood of geopolitical disruptions affecting energy production and transit.

variables.name: Diplomatic negotiation intensity
variables.description: Frequency and vigor of diplomatic and intergovernmental negotiations aimed at securing access to energy resources.

variables.name: Maritime security tension
variables.description: Level of tension and potential disruption in key maritime transit corridors for oil shipments.

variables.name: Domestic political backlash intensity
variables.description: Strength of domestic political opposition and public protest directed at foreign involvement in national energy assets.

variables.name: Contractual enforcement strength
variables.description: Effective strength of legal and judicial mechanisms to uphold and enforce contracts related to energy assets.

variables.name: International sanction pressure
variables.description: Degree of external economic and regulatory pressure applied through sanctions that constrain energy transactions.

variables.name: Investor confidence in energy deals
variables.description: Perceived willingness of private and institutional investors to commit capital to energy agreements in the jurisdiction.

variables.name: Regulatory expropriation risk
variables.description: Probability that host-jurisdiction regulatory or political actions will seize, nullify, or materially alter ownership of energy assets.

variables.name: Capital flow to oil sector
variables.description: Net financial flows (equity, loans, and investments) directed into upstream oil exploration and production activities.

variables.name: Strategic value of reserves
variables.description: Geopolitical and economic importance attributed to a jurisdiction's oil reserves as a strategic resource.

catalysts.title: Formal US–Venezuela oil agreement signing
catalysts.description: A formal, ratified agreement or memorandum of understanding is signed, defining US access/control terms over Venezuelan oil assets.
catalysts.rationale: News reporting US nears deal and Trump announces deal to secure Venezuelan reserves [2026-08-28/29].

catalysts.title: Chevron deal completion on Venezuelan projects
catalysts.description: Chevron completes contractual migration/expansion of projects in Venezuela, formalising operational roles and investments.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines state Chevron to complete deal and U.S. firms near investments in Venezuelan fields [2026-08-29].

catalysts.title: U.S. firms' investment ramp-up into Venezuelan fields
catalysts.description: Staged capital deployments and project funding by Chevron and other U.S. firms ramp up investment into Venezuelan upstream assets.
catalysts.rationale: Reports say Chevron and other U.S. firms are near deals to invest billions in Venezuelan oil fields [2026-08-29].

catalysts.title: Domestic political backlash in Venezuela
catalysts.description: Sustained denouncements, protests, and political opposition in Venezuela target the US-linked oil deal, risking disruptions and policy reversals.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Oil deal with US is denounced by both sides of Venezuelan politics' [2026-08-30].

catalysts.title: International sanctions and legal challenges
catalysts.description: Third-party states or multilateral actors initiate sanctions, litigation, or legal actions challenging transfers of Venezuelan oil control.
catalysts.rationale: Announcements of US control and denouncements imply likely international legal/sanction responses [2026-08-28/30].

catalysts.title: Iran–Oman Strait of Hormuz transit deal progress
catalysts.description: An emergent Iran–Oman arrangement affecting Strait of Hormuz transit rules reduces chokepoint tensions and market risk perceptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran and Oman edge towards deal on Strait of Hormuz' and market reaction in oil settles lower [2026-08-28/29].
